ownerThemes.theme: Owners like getting a 5-thread serger and coverstitch in one box for roughly $450 to $650 and report clean stitches once set up.
In coverstitch mode there is little room under the foot; pressing the lifter bar further down helps slide fabric in. Some report the right needle skipping and the triple cover never forming.
Singer 2022 needles are required and hard to find, especially size 11; threading is described as difficult until learned.

editorial.verdict: A 5-thread serger and coverstitch in one box at 1,300 spm, with a manual changeover each time you switch and many owner threads about threading trouble.
editorial.whoFor: A sewist short on space or budget who wants a 5-thread safety stitch and coverstitch in one machine and accepts a changeover between modes.
editorial.skipIf: You switch between seaming and hemming often in one project, or want a stated free arm or thread trimmer; Singer publishes neither.
editorial.keySpec: 2/3/4/5 thread · serger + coverstitch · 1,300 spm · 3.0 to 9.8 mm width · 19.84 lb
strengths: Singer lists 14 stitches with 2 to 5 thread capability and a coverstitch in one machine, which the 14HD854 and 14CG754 pages do not offer.
Singer's manual publishes the working ranges: differential feed 1:0.6 to 1:2.0, overedge width 3.0 to 9.8 mm, stitch length 1 to 4 mm, presser foot rise 4.5 mm.
Owners report pleasing cover stitch and general stitch results in some threads, and Sewing Machines Plus shows 4.78 from 9 reviews (a small sample).
weaknesses: Owners report threading and looper trouble across 21 statements, including looper threads that never interlock and painful frequent switching between serger and coverstitch.
Owners report defects and skipped stitches in 15 statements, mostly from help-seeking Reddit threads, so this is not a failure rate.
Owners report the auto tension dial still needs adjusting, and Singer's manual says to adjust in small steps if results differ.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Singer 14T968DC?
faqs.a: Reports are split. Some owners report clean stitches once it is set up and some call it sturdy, while the loudest complaints are threading and looper trouble (21 voices, 20 of them owners), skipped or bunched stitches, and tension that still needs adjusting. The read covers 32 Reddit threads and 2 retailer pages from 2010 to 2026. Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: How hard is the Singer 14T968DC to thread?
faqs.a: Owners say threading is the hard part: 21 voices, 20 of them owners, mention threading or the loopers, and 9 of those statements are negative. One owner reports the upper and lower looper threads never crossing in serger mode despite repeated rethreading. Singer describes color-coded threading and the manual covers it, so follow the manual diagram for each mode.

faqs.q: What needles does the Singer 14T968DC use?
faqs.a: Singer 2022 (EL x 705), with size 14/90 supplied. The manual says to use only 14/90 and 11/80 and warns against standard household needles. Cover stitch needle gauges are 2.8 mm (narrow) and 5.6 mm (wide and triple). One PatternReview owner says the 2022 needles are hard to find, especially size 11.

faqs.q: How long does it take to switch the Singer 14T968DC between serger and coverstitch?
faqs.a: Singer does not publish a changeover time, so it is [verify]. The manual covers sewing a cover stitch with a clutch change and cover stitch needles. Owners in our read describe frequent switching between serger and coverstitch as painful, so plan your sewing in batches.

faqs.q: Does the Singer 14T968DC do a 5-thread overlock?
faqs.a: Singer lists 2, 3, 4 or 5 thread capability and 14 built-in stitches, and its manual lists 2/3/4/5-thread overlock. Singer does not use the words safety stitch in the figures we recorded, so confirm that in the manual before you buy [verify]. Threading is where owners struggle, so expect a learning period on the 5-thread setup.

faqs.q: Does the Singer 14T968DC have a free arm or a thread trimmer?
faqs.a: Singer's page and manual do not state a free arm, and neither publishes a thread trimmer, so both are [verify]. The knife trims the fabric edge only. Singer's 14CG754 page does state a built-in free arm, so do not assume it carries over to this model.

faqs.q: Why does the Singer 14T968DC skip stitches?
faqs.a: Owners report it: one describes skipped stitches on a 3-thread overlock after four needle changes, and another reports cover stitch K bunching at looper A despite rethreading. Defects and skipped stitches are 15 voices, mostly from help-seeking Reddit threads, so this is not a failure rate. Singer's manual allows only Singer 2022 needles in 14/90 and 11/80, so check the needle first.

faqs.q: How much does the Singer 14T968DC weigh?
faqs.a: Singer's manual gives 9.0 kg, which is 19.84 lb. Singer's product page shows 18.6 with no unit, so the sources disagree. We use the manual figure.

faqs.q: Is the tension on the Singer 14T968DC really automatic?
faqs.a: Singer calls it a self-adjusting tension system, but the manual shows an Auto Tension Dial that you set per stitch. The automatic settings are based on medium weight fabric and standard 60 polyester spun thread, with small adjustments if results differ. One owner calls the auto tension frustrating, and 11 voices in our read discuss tension.
